questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.**

To be light years away

options.text: To be too distant for human beings to reach
An unlikely event that happened suddenly
An extremely long time from now in the past or future
When something seems like it is about to happen in the near future

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. To be too distant for human beings to reach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To be light years away"** means to refer to something that is extremely far away or distant, usually beyond the reach of human beings. (बहुत दूर होना)

 
 
• **Example: **Technological advancements that we can only dream of now might be light years away.
 
 
 
• Option 1 **"To be too distant for human beings to reach"** accurately captures this meaning. ( मनुष्यों के पहुंच से बहुत दूर)
 
 
• **Example: **Exploring galaxies beyond our Milky Way is light years away in terms of current space travel technology.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of the idiom "To be light years away" is best matched by option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2** An unlikely event that happened suddenly (असंभव घटना जो अचानक घटित हो गई)

 
 
• **Example:** Winning the lottery is an unlikely event that happened suddenly.
 
 
 
• **Option 3** An extremely long time from now in the past or future (अत्यधिक लंबे समय से अब या भविष्य में)
 
 
• **Example: ** The extinction of dinosaurs happened light years ago.
 
 
 
• **Option 4** When something seems like it is about to happen in the near future (जब कुछ ऐसा होता है कि भविष्य में होने वाला है)
 
 
• **Example:** The launch of the new product is about to happen in the near future.

options.text: Show someone how to do a job or activity
Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom **'Steer clear of'** is **'Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you'.**
 
• **Steer clear of:** to avoid something or someone. (कुछ या किसी से बचने के लिए)
 
 
• *Example: After her bad experience with the previous employer, she decided to **steer clear of** any company with a similar work culture.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Answer:__** *Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the origin of this idiom:
 
 
• The idiom** "steer clear of"** has its origin in **nautical terminology**. The word "**steer**" in this phrase refers to the act of steering a ship, and "**clear**" means to navigate around or avoid any **obstacles** that may come in the ship's way.
 
• In the context of sailing, the phrase** "steer clear of" **was used as a warning to sailors to avoid any objects or vessels that could potentially cause damage to their ships. If a captain wanted to avoid a collision with another ship or object, he would give the order to** "steer clear of"** it, which meant that the ship's course should be changed to avoid the obstacle.
 
• Over time, the phrase** "steer clear of" **came to be used in a broader sense, beyond the world of sailing. It began to be used as a metaphor for avoiding or staying away from any situation or person that could cause trouble or harm. The phrase has become a part of everyday language and is widely used in modern English to advise or warn someone to avoid a situation or person.
